changelog: Replace E1 with labeled example en_us_48 to teach the scorer about high-contra single cuts that kill set quality (addresses the primary finding that entailment risk is underweighted).
Replace E2 with labeled example en_us_1081 to illustrate a ≤5-bin case where a single high-contra cut must be ranked low despite apparent cohesion (covers mid-low latency loss).
Replace E4 with labeled example en_us_455 to show another ≤3-bin instance where keeping a cohesive-looking but highly-contradictory cut harms overall set score.
findings: The scorer underweights entailment (contra) risk when a cut looks cohesive: it ranks positions that produce a high standalone contradiction too highly, letting a single kept cut 'kill' the set even though avoiding that one cut would rescue quality.
The scorer applies 'avoid cutting near heads / between predicate and arguments' too broadly, thinning segmentations in very short-latency regimes where dense safe cuts are needed.

diagnosis.why: Replacing the examples to teach the scorer about single high-contradiction cuts caused it to downrank those specific high-contra boundaries (producing modest average gains, especially in the ≤7 bin) but in many short-latency cases it compensated by preferring alternative splits that fragment noun phrases and enumerations, producing numerous local losses.
diagnosis.lesson: A later revision should avoid fixing single high-contra cuts by encouraging alternative fragmenting splits — preserve noun-phrase and enumeration integrity in short-latency (≤3–≤5) cases when de-emphasizing high-contradiction single cuts.
